title: The GCaMP3 – A GFP-based calcium sensor for imaging calcium dynamics in the human malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum
author: Borges-Pereira, Campos, et al.

steps.title: Clone GCaMP3 into pDC vector
steps.instruction: Amplify the GCaMP3 ORF from the mammalian plasmid, clone into pJET, subclone into pDC, and verify orientation and sequence.

substeps.instruction: Set up PCR with ~100 ng template plasmid, primers 5′‑GGATCCATGGGTTCTCATCATCATCATC‑3′ and 5′‑GGATCCTTACTTCGCTGTCATCATTTGTAC‑3′ (BamHI sites added), using 94 °C 5′, then 34 cycles of 95 °C 55″, 50 °C 60″, 68 °C 180″, and a final 74 °C 5′; expected amplicon ≈1.3 kb.
Purify the PCR product from agarose gel with PureLink™ Quick Gel Extraction Kit (Invitrogen) following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Ligate the purified amplicon into the bacterial propagation vector pJET (Fermentas) and transform One Shot® TOP10 chemically competent E. coli (Invitrogen) by heat‑shock.
Plate transformants on LB agar containing ampicillin and incubate at 37 °C for 20 h; pick single colonies and grow each in 5 mL LB/ampicillin at 37 °C, 180 rpm for 20 h.
Extract plasmid DNA from each culture using Wizard® Plus SV Minipreps DNA Purification System (Promega).

Digest each miniprep with BamHI (~10 U enzyme) at 37 °C for 2 h to confirm insertion of the ~1.3 kb GCaMP3 fragment; verify by gel electrophoresis and sequence the insert (identical to synthetic GCaMP3, GI: 299818412).

Digest the confirmed pJET/GCaMP3 plasmid and the P. falciparum transfection vector pDC (provided by Dr. Gerhard Wunderlich) with BamHI; purify the ~1.3 kb GCaMP3 fragment and the ~6 kb pDC backbone from agarose gel.
Ligate the BamHI‑digested fragments at 16 °C overnight.

Transform the ligation mix into chemically competent E. coli (heat‑shock), plate, and incubate; from 12 colonies, screen by colony PCR and BamHI/XhoI digests. Colonies 8 and 11 contain the insert; XhoI digestion shows correct orientation.
Select colony 11 for plasmid preparation and confirm the sequence matches the synthetic GCaMP3 construct.

steps.title: Electroporate P. falciparum with construct
steps.instruction: Introduce the pDC/GCaMP3 plasmid into synchronized ring‑stage parasites and apply drug selection.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a synchronized ring‑stage culture at ~10 % parasitemia; harvest 200 µL of infected erythrocytes.
Resuspend cells in 500 µL Cytomix buffer (120 mM KCl, 0.15 mM CaCl₂, 2 mM EGTA, 5 mM MgCl₂, 10 mM K₂HPO₄/KH₂PO₄, 25 mM HEPES).
Add 50 µg of the purified pDC/GCaMP3 plasmid to the suspension and transfer to a 0.4‑cm electroporation cuvette.
Electroporate using 2.5 kV, 25 µF, 200 Ω; keep the cuvette on ice for 5 min post‑pulse.
Transfer the electroporated cells to a culture flask containing 10 mL RPMI‑1640 (Gibco) supplemented with 0.5 % albumax, 2 g L⁻¹ sodium bicarbonate, 40 mg L⁻¹ gentamicin, and 50 mg L⁻¹ hypoxanthine.
Incubate at 5 % CO₂, 5 % O₂, 90 % N₂.
After 48 h add 5 nM WR99210 to select for transformants.
Maintain cultures; fluorescent transfectants typically appear after ~2 weeks and can be visualized by fluorescence microscopy.

steps.title: Select and enrich transfected parasites
steps.instruction: Isolate fluorescent parasites by flow sorting, clone by limiting dilution, and verify by LDH activity.

substeps.instruction: Sort the culture on a BD FACSAria II™ cell sorter (488 nm excitation) to collect cells with increased fluorescence intensity.
Culture the sorted population for 1 week.
Clone the parasites by limiting dilution in 96‑well plates at 0.5 parasite per well.
After ~2 weeks, assay each well for parasite growth by measuring lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) activity:
Prepare Malstat reagent: dissolve 400 µL Triton X‑100 in 80 mL deionized water, add 4.00 g L‑lactate, 1.32 g Tris buffer, 0.022 g APAD; adjust to pH 9 and bring to 200 mL total volume.
Prepare NBT/PES solution: dissolve 0.160 g nitro‑blue tetrazolium (NBT) and 0.008 g phenazine ethosulfate (PES) in 100 mL deionized water.
Take 15 µL of culture from each well, add to a plate containing 100 µL Malstat reagent and 25 µL NBT/PES solution; incubate and read absorbance at 620 nm.
Select the clone showing the highest percentage of fluorescent parasites for downstream experiments.

steps.title: Measure calcium response of PfGCaMP3
steps.instruction: Stimulate parasites with ionomycin and record GCaMP3 fluorescence by flow cytometry.

substeps.instruction: Harvest the chosen fluorescent clone at the trophozoite stage; centrifuge infected erythrocytes at 2000 rpm for 5 min.
Wash the pellet twice with buffer A (per litre: 116 mM NaCl, 5.4 mM KCl, 0.8 mM MgSO₄, 5.5 mM d‑glucose, 50 mM MOPS, 2 mM CaCl₂).
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL buffer A, add 2 µM ionomycin, and incubate for 1 min.
Acquire 1 × 10⁵ cells on a FACS Calibur flow cytometer using CELLQUEST software; excite GCaMP3 with a 488 nm argon laser and collect emission at 520–530 nm.
Analyze side‑scatter versus fluorescence dot plots to quantify calcium‑induced fluorescence changes.
